selected_evidence.summary: `opsbot` exists on both nodes; key files have correct ownership and permissions; authorized-key fingerprints match node1's generated key.
Effective sshd policy requires `publickey`; live key logins succeed on both nodes, while password-only attempts fail.
Shows healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, restored sshd listener, persisted account/key/policy, and successful post-restart key logins.

Shows healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, restored sshd listener, persisted account/key/policy, successful post-restart key access from node1, and continued password rejection.

commands.command:
set -eu; if ! id opsbot >/dev/null 2>&1; then useradd -m -s /bin/bash opsbot; fi; passwd -l opsbot >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; install -d -m 700 -o opsbot -g opsbot /home/opsbot/.ssh; if [ ! -f /home/opsbot/.ssh/id_ed25519 ]; then runuser -u opsbot -- ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -f /home/opsbot/.ssh/id_ed25519; fi; install -m 600 -o opsbot -g opsbot /home/opsbot/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub /home/opsbot/.ssh/authorized_keys; printf 'Match User opsbot
    PubkeyAuthentication yes
    PasswordAuthentication no
    KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
    AuthenticationMethods publickey
' > /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/90-opsbot-key-only.conf; chmod 600 /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/90-opsbot-key-only.conf; sshd -t; systemctl reload sshd; id opsbot; passwd -S opsbot; stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' /home/opsbot/.ssh /home/opsbot/.ssh/id_ed25519 /home/opsbot/.ssh/authorized_keys; ssh-keygen -lf /home/opsbot/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
